newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's balance of payments on target - Ortiz.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's balance of payments on target - Ortiz.

text.p: Mexico's balance of payments so far this year has been in line with government year-end objectives, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said in an interview published Tuesday.

"With respect to the balance of payments, the results of the first two months of the year are totally congruent with the result expected for the end of the year -- a deficit in the current account of less than two percent of the gross domestic product (around $5.5 billion) which will be fully financed by the direct foreign investment expected this year," Ortiz told the daily El Financiero.
In answer to a question referring to business warnings that the country's balance of payments was going askew, Ortiz was adamant. "I do not see any problem on the balance of payments front," he said.

On the country's trade balance, he was equally firm. "We are not going over the line in terms of the trade balance. Results show we are going according to plan, exports keep growing vigorously, although at lesser rates," he added, not mentioning imports.
Mexico has reported monthly trade surpluses to February this year, but analysts widely predict the country will slip into monthly deficits in the second half as import growth outpaces exports.
